en autostol.explanation: "En autostol" means "a car seat". It is built from "auto" (car) and "stol" (chair).

en avis.explanation: "En avis" means "a newspaper". To say you have a regular delivery that you pay for, use "abonnere på" (to subscribe to): "Vi abonnerer på en avis" (We subscribe to a newspaper).

en avocado.explanation: "En avocado" means "an avocado". To say it is ripe, use "moden" (ripe): "Avocadoen er moden" (The avocado is ripe).

et abonnement.explanation: "Et abonnement" means "a subscription". To say you start one, use "tegne" (to take out): "Jeg vil gerne tegne et abonnement" (I would like to take out a subscription).

et adgangskrav.explanation: "Et adgangskrav" means "an admission requirement". It is built from "adgang" (access) and "krav" (demand). To say you meet it, use "opfylde" (to fulfil): "Hun opfylder adgangskravet" (She meets the admission requirement).

et afslag.explanation: "Et afslag" means "a refusal". When you talk about a lower price, it means "a price reduction": "Vi fik et afslag i prisen" (We got a reduction in the price).

et afsnit.explanation: "Et afsnit" means "an episode". When you count what you watched, say: "Jeg har set tre afsnit" (I have watched three episodes). When you talk about a text, it means "a section": "Læs det første afsnit" (Read the first section).

et agern.explanation: "Et agern" means "an acorn". Do not mix it up with "et egern" (a squirrel). To say an acorn lies somewhere: "Der ligger et agern på jorden" (There is an acorn on the ground). To say a squirrel is somewhere: "Der sidder et egern i træet" (There is a squirrel in the tree).

et aktieselskab.explanation: "Et aktieselskab" means "a public limited company". It is built from "aktie" (share) and "selskab" (company). In a company name, the short form is "A/S": "Carlsberg A/S".

et akvarium.explanation: "Et akvarium" means "an aquarium". When you talk about a place you visit with many large tanks, it also means "an aquarium": "Vi så hajer i akvariet" (We saw sharks in the aquarium).

et alarmnummer.explanation: "Et alarmnummer" means "an emergency number". It is built from "alarm" (alarm) and "nummer" (number).

et album.explanation: "Et album" means "an album". To talk about photos, put "foto" (photo) in front: "et fotoalbum" (a photo album).

et alfabet.explanation: "Et alfabet" means "an alphabet". A fact about Denmark: the Danish alphabet has 29 letters. To say things are in alphabetical order, use "alfabetisk" (alphabetical): "Ordene står i alfabetisk rækkefølge" (The words are in alphabetical order).

et alibi.explanation: "Et alibi" means "an alibi". When you talk about an excuse, it also means "an excuse": "Hun brugte travlheden som alibi" (She used being busy as an excuse).

et alternativ.explanation: "Et alternativ" means "an alternative". To say there is no other choice, say: "Der er intet alternativ" (There is no alternative). When you describe something as different from the normal kind, it works as an adjective: "alternativ medicin" (alternative medicine).

et anførselstegn.explanation: "Et anførselstegn" means "a quotation mark". It is also called "gåseøjne" (literally, goose eyes). To say you put a word between quotation marks, say: "Skriv ordet i anførselstegn" (Write the word in quotation marks).

et angreb.explanation: "Et angreb" means "an attack". It comes from the verb "at angribe" (to attack). To say someone starts attacking, use "gå til angreb" (to go on the attack): "Soldaterne gik til angreb" (The soldiers went on the attack).

et anker.explanation: "Et anker" means "an anchor". To say a ship pulls up its anchor and leaves, use "lette anker" (to weigh anchor): "Skibet letter anker" (The ship weighs anchor).

et anlæg.explanation: "Et anlæg" means "a facility / plant". To name a specific kind of facility, put a word in front: "et idrætsanlæg" (a sports facility).

et anpartsselskab.explanation: "Et anpartsselskab" means "a private limited company". It is built from "anpart" (share) and "selskab" (company). In a company name, the short form is "ApS": "Café Sol ApS".

et ansigt.explanation: "Et ansigt" means "a face". To say people meet in person, use "ansigt til ansigt" (face to face): "Vi mødtes ansigt til ansigt" (We met face to face).

et ansigtstræk.explanation: "Et ansigtstræk" means "a facial feature". Do not mix it up with "et ansigtsudtryk" (a facial expression). To talk about a part of the face, use "ansigtstræk": "Hans næse er et tydeligt ansigtstræk" (His nose is a clear facial feature). To talk about the look on a face, use "ansigtsudtryk": "Hun fik et vredt ansigtsudtryk" (She got an angry facial expression).

et ansigtsudtryk.explanation: "Et ansigtsudtryk" means "a facial expression". To say what the expression is like, put a describing word in front: "et glad ansigtsudtryk" (a happy facial expression).

et ansvar.explanation: "Et ansvar" means "a responsibility". To say someone accepts it, use "tage" (to take): "Han tager ansvar for fejlen" (He takes responsibility for the mistake).

et antal.explanation: "Et antal" means "a number (amount)", as in how many. When you talk about how many guests came, say: "Antallet af gæster var lille" (The number of guests was small). Do not mix it up with "et tal" (a number). When you talk about the number 5 itself, use "et tal": "Fem er et tal" (Five is a number).

et apotek.explanation: "Et apotek" means "a pharmacy". To say where you are going, use "på" (at): "Jeg skal på apoteket" (I have to go to the pharmacy).

et apparat.explanation: "Et apparat" means "a device". To name a specific kind of device, put a word in front: "et høreapparat" (a hearing aid).

et ar.explanation: "Et ar" means "a scar". Do not mix it up with "et år" (a year), which has a little ring over the "å". To talk about a scar: "Såret blev til et ar" (The wound became a scar). To talk about a year: "Et år har tolv måneder" (A year has twelve months).

et arbejde.explanation: "Et arbejde" means "a job / work". To say you are at your workplace, use "på arbejde" (at work): "Jeg er på arbejde" (I am at work).

et arbejdsmiljø.explanation: "Et arbejdsmiljø" means "a work environment". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "miljø" (environment). In Denmark, "Arbejdstilsynet" (the Danish Working Environment Authority) is the authority that checks the work environment.

et areal.explanation: "Et areal" means "an area", as in the size of a surface. To ask how big a room is, say: "Hvad er rummets areal?" (What is the area of the room?) Do not mix it up with "et område" (an area as a region). To talk about a region, say: "Der er mange parker i området" (There are many parks in the area).

et argument.explanation: "Et argument" means "an argument", as in a reason for your view. To ask for someone's reason, say: "Hvad er dit argument?" (What is your argument?) Do not mix it up with "et skænderi" (a quarrel). To say two people had a quarrel: "De havde et skænderi i går" (They had a quarrel yesterday).

et arkiv.explanation: "Et arkiv" means "an archive". To name what is stored, put a word in front: "et fotoarkiv" (a photo archive).

et armbåndsur.explanation: "Et armbåndsur" means "a wristwatch". It is built from "armbånd" (bracelet) and "ur" (watch or clock).

et askebæger.explanation: "Et askebæger" means "an ashtray". It ends in "bæger" (cup), as in "et æggebæger" (an egg cup).

et aspekt.explanation: "Et aspekt" means "an aspect". To say which part matters most, say: "Det vigtigste aspekt er prisen" (The most important aspect is the price).

et atom.explanation: "Et atom" means "an atom". It is the first part of "atomkraft" (nuclear power) and "atombombe" (atomic bomb).

et auditorium.explanation: "Et auditorium" means "an auditorium / lecture hall". To say where you meet for a lecture: "Vi mødes i auditoriet" (We meet in the lecture hall).

et autoværksted.explanation: "Et autoværksted" means "a car repair shop". It is built from "auto" (car) and "værksted" (workshop), which also appears in "et cykelværksted" (a bike repair shop).

at åbne.explanation: "At åbne" means "to open". To ask a shop when it opens, say: "Hvornår åbner I?" (When do you open?)

at åbne op.explanation: "At åbne op" means "to open up". When you mean to make something possible, use "åbne op for": "Det åbner op for nye muligheder" (It opens up new possibilities).

at ånde.explanation: "At ånde" means "to breathe". To say you cannot breathe, use "trække vejret" (literally, to pull the breath): "Jeg kan ikke trække vejret" (I cannot breathe).

en å.explanation: "En å" means "a stream", as in flowing water. To talk about a stream: "Der er fisk i åen" (There are fish in the stream). Do not mix it up with "en flod" (a river). To talk about a big river: "Floden er meget bred" (The river is very wide).

en åbning.explanation: "En åbning" means "an opening". When you talk about the start of an event, it also means "an opening": "Åbningen af udstillingen er i morgen" (The opening of the exhibition is tomorrow).

en åbningsdag.explanation: "En åbningsdag" means "an opening day". It is built from "åbning" (opening) and "dag" (day).

en åbningstid.explanation: "En åbningstid" means "an opening hour". To ask when a shop is open, use the plural "åbningstider": "Hvad er butikkens åbningstider?" (What are the shop's opening hours?)

en åkande.explanation: "En åkande" means "a water lily". To name its leaf, add "blad" (leaf): "et åkandeblad" (a water lily leaf).

en ål.explanation: "En ål" means "an eel". Do not mix it up with "en å" (a stream). To talk about an eel: "Vi fangede en ål" (We caught an eel). To talk about a stream: "Åen er smal" (The stream is narrow).

en ånd.explanation: "En ånd" means "a spirit", as in a being without a body. When you talk about the main idea behind something, it means "the spirit": "lovens ånd" (the spirit of the law).

en årring.explanation: "En årring" means "a tree ring". To say how to find the age of a tree, use "tælle" (to count): "Man tæller årringene for at finde træets alder" (You count the tree rings to find the age of the tree).

en årsag.explanation: "En årsag" means "a reason", as in the cause of something. To name a cause, say: "Årsagen til branden er ukendt" (The reason for the fire is unknown). Do not mix it up with "en grund" (a reason). To give a reason for doing something, use "grund": "Jeg har en god grund til at blive hjemme" (I have a good reason to stay home).

en årsopgørelse.explanation: "En årsopgørelse" means "an annual tax statement". It is built from "år" (year) and "opgørelse" (statement). A fact about Denmark: the Danish tax authorities send one to every taxpayer.

en årstid.explanation: "En årstid" means "a season". To name your favorite, say: "Efteråret er min yndlingsårstid" (Autumn is my favorite season). Do not mix it up with "en sæson" (a season of a show or sport): "Sæsonen starter i dag" (The season starts today).

et åbent hus.explanation: "Et åbent hus" means "an open house". When a house is for sale and buyers may visit, it also means "an open house": "Der er åbent hus søndag klokken to" (There is an open house on Sunday at two o'clock).

et år.explanation: "Et år" means "a year". To say your age, add "gammel" (old): "Jeg er tredive år gammel" (I am thirty years old).

et århundrede.explanation: "Et århundrede" means "a century". It is built from "år" (year) and "hundrede" (hundred). To name a period, use a number with a dot: "i det 21. århundrede" (in the 21st century).

et årstal.explanation: "Et årstal" means "a year (date)". To say that a number is a year: "1990 er et årstal" (1990 is a year). Do not mix it up with "et år" (a year as a length of time). To say how long: "tre år" (three years).

et årti.explanation: "Et årti" means "a decade". To name a decade, add "-erne" to the number: "firserne" (the eighties).

åben.explanation: "Åben" means "open". To talk about the action, use the verb "at åbne" (to open): "Jeg åbner døren" (I open the door).

åbenbart.explanation: "Åbenbart" means "apparently". It comes from the word "åbenbar" (obvious). To say you have just noticed something, say: "Du har åbenbart ikke hørt det" (You have apparently not heard it).

åbenlys.explanation: "Åbenlys" means "obvious". It is built from "åben" (open) and "lys" (light). To say something is clearly true, say: "Det er åbenlyst, at hun har ret" (It is obvious that she is right).

åbningstider.explanation: "Åbningstider" means "opening hours". It is built from "åbning" (opening) and "tider" (times).

åndelig.explanation: "Åndelig" means "spiritual". It comes from "en ånd" (a spirit). To say someone looks for spiritual help, say: "Han søger åndelig vejledning" (He seeks spiritual guidance). Do not mix it up with "psykisk" (mental). To talk about the mind, say: "Hun har psykiske problemer" (She has mental problems).

årlig.explanation: "Årlig" means "annual". To say how often something happens, use "årligt" (annually): "Det sker årligt" (It happens every year).

årvågen.explanation: "Årvågen" means "alert". The last part, "vågen" (awake), also stands alone: "Jeg er vågen" (I am awake).

at æde.explanation: "At æde" means "to eat (of animals)". To say an animal eats, say: "Løven æder kød" (The lion eats meat). For people, use "at spise" (to eat): "Jeg spiser frokost" (I eat lunch). Said about a person, "æde" sounds coarse.

at ændre.explanation: "At ændre" means "to change / alter". To say someone has a new opinion, say: "Hun har ændret mening" (She has changed her mind). To swap one thing for another, use "at skifte" (to change, to swap): "Jeg skifter dæk" (I change tires).

at ændre på.explanation: "At ændre på" means "to change something". To ask for permission to change a part, say: "Må jeg ændre på teksten?" (May I change the text?) To become different by itself, use "at ændre sig" (to change): "Vejret ændrer sig" (The weather is changing).

at ændre sig.explanation: "At ændre sig" means "to change". To say a person is different now, say: "Hun har ændret sig meget" (She has changed a lot). To change something else, leave out "sig": "Jeg ændrer planen" (I change the plan).

at ærgre sig.explanation: "At ærgre sig" means "to be annoyed". To say what annoys you, add "over" (about): "Jeg ærgrer mig over, at jeg kom for sent" (I am annoyed that I was late).

en æblekage.explanation: "En æblekage" means "an apple dessert". A fact about Denmark: it is made of stewed apple, crumbs and whipped cream layered in a glass. It is built from "æble" (apple) and "kage" (cake), but it is not baked as a cake.

en æggejagt.explanation: "En æggejagt" means "an egg hunt". It is built from "æg" (egg) and "jagt" (hunt).

en æggemad.explanation: "En æggemad" means "an egg open sandwich". A fact about Denmark: it is a slice of bread with sliced boiled egg on top. The word "mad" also ends "en ostemad" (a cheese sandwich).

en ægtefælle.explanation: "En ægtefælle" means "a spouse". It is built from "ægte" (genuine) and "fælle" (companion). To ask for a spouse's name, say: "Hvad er din ægtefælles navn?" (What is your spouse's name?)

en ægtemand.explanation: "En ægtemand" means "a husband". It is built from "ægte" (genuine) and "mand" (man). To say "my husband" in a shorter way, say "min mand": "Min mand er hjemme" (My husband is home).

en ælling.explanation: "En ælling" means "a duckling". A fact about Denmark: "Den grimme ælling" (The Ugly Duckling) is a fairy tale by H.C. Andersen.

en ændring.explanation: "En ændring" means "a change". To say you make a change, use "lave" (to make): "Jeg laver en ændring i planen" (I am making a change in the plan). To swap one thing for another, say "at skifte" (to switch): "at skifte sko" (to change shoes).

en æske.explanation: "En æske" means "a box". To name what is inside, put it after "æske": "en æske tændstikker" (a box of matches). Do not mix it up with "en kasse" (a crate / large box): "en kasse øl" (a crate of beer).

et æble.explanation: "Et æble" means "an apple". To name a food made from apples, join "æble" with another word: "æblekage" (apple dessert).

et æg.explanation: "Et æg" means "an egg". To say how an egg is cooked, add "kogt" (boiled): "et kogt æg" (a boiled egg). A fried egg has its own word, "et spejlæg" (literally, a mirror egg).

et æggebæger.explanation: "Et æggebæger" means "an egg cup". It is built from "æg" (egg) and "bæger" (cup). The word "bæger" is also in "et yoghurtbæger" (a yogurt cup).

et ægtepar.explanation: "Et ægtepar" means "a married couple". To say two people are married: "De er et ægtepar" (They are a married couple). Two people who are together but not married are "et kærestepar" (a couple): "De er et kærestepar" (They are a couple).

et ægteskab.explanation: "Et ægteskab" means "a marriage". Do not mix it up with "et bryllup" (a wedding). To talk about the marriage: "Deres ægteskab er lykkeligt" (Their marriage is happy). To talk about the ceremony: "Deres bryllup er i dag" (Their wedding is today).

et ærinde.explanation: "Et ærinde" means "an errand". To say you go out to do one, use "løbe" (to run): "Jeg løber lige et ærinde" (I am just running an errand). To ask why someone has come to a door or desk, it also means "business": "Hvad er dit ærinde?" (What is your business here?)

et ærme.explanation: "Et ærme" means "a sleeve". To say you start working hard, use "smøge" (to roll up): "Vi smøger ærmerne op" (We roll up our sleeves).

et æsel.explanation: "Et æsel" means "a donkey". To say someone is very stubborn: "Han er stædig som et æsel" (He is as stubborn as a donkey).

ædel.explanation: "Ædel" means "noble". In names of valuable materials, it means "precious": "ædelmetal" (precious metal).

ædru.explanation: "Ædru" means "sober". To warn someone about driving, say: "Kør ikke, hvis du ikke er ædru" (Do not drive if you are not sober).

ægte.explanation: "Ægte" means "genuine". It is also the first part of "ægtefælle" (spouse) and "ægteskab" (marriage).

ældgammel.explanation: "Ældgammel" means "ancient". It ends in "gammel" (old). To say a custom goes far back in time: "en ældgammel skik" (an ancient custom).

ældre.explanation: "Ældre" means "elderly". It is also the form of "gammel" (old) that means "older". To talk about elderly people as a group, say "de ældre" (the elderly): "Vi besøger de ældre" (We visit the elderly).

ældst.explanation: "Ældst" means "oldest". It follows the pattern "gammel" (old), "ældre" (older), "ældst" (oldest). To point to one person, say: "Hun er den ældste" (She is the oldest).

ære.explanation: "En ære" means "an honor". To say something is done to honor someone, use "til ære for" (in honor of): "en fest til ære for hende" (a party in honor of her).

ærefuld.explanation: "Ærefuld" means "honorable". It is built from "ære" (honor) and "-fuld" (full of).

æret.explanation: "Æret" means "honored". To open a speech politely, use the plural "ærede": "Ærede gæster!" (Honored guests!)

ærgerlig.explanation: "Ærgerlig" means "unfortunate". To say you are sorry that something did not work out: "Det er ærgerligt, at du ikke kan komme" (It is a shame you cannot come).

ærgerrig.explanation: "Ærgerrig" means "ambitious". To say a person is ambitious: "Hun er meget ærgerrig" (She is very ambitious). Do not mix it up with "ærgerlig" (a pity). To say something is a pity: "Det er ærgerligt" (That is a pity).

ærlig.explanation: "Ærlig" means "honest". To ask someone to tell the truth, say: "Vær ærlig!" (Be honest!) To start a frank remark, say "ærligt talt" (honestly): "Ærligt talt, jeg kan ikke lide det" (Honestly, I do not like it).
